title: “TAKE YOUR SON.”
paragraphs:
Not your flock.
Not your silver.
Not your future plans.

Your only son.
The one you waited twenty-five years to hold.
Dawn had barely touched the hills when Book of Genesis chapter 22 opens with words that shake the bones of faith:
“Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love… and offer him there as a burnt offering.” (Genesis 22:2)

The mountain air thin.
The wood on Isaac’s shoulders.
The knife hidden in Abraham’s robe.
Three days of questions echoing inside a father’s chest.

“Father… we have the fire and the wood.
But where is the lamb?”
The question every trembling believer asks when obedience hurts.
Abraham answers with a whisper of faith:
And somehow—somewhere between trust and tears—Isaac is bound.
Faith has reached its breaking point.
“Do not lay a hand on the boy.”
And the mountain receives a name:
This story was never only about Abraham.
Because centuries later, on another hill in the land of Mount Moriah’s region, another Father would give His only Son.
That Son would carry the wood of His own sacrifice.
No angel would stop the knife.

Jesus Christ did what Isaac never had to do—
He died so sinners could live.
Maybe today your faith feels like Abraham’s climb.
But the mountain of testing is often the place where God reveals His provision.
If you’re carrying something that feels impossible to surrender…
Grace has already met you on the mountain.

Repent.
Trust Christ.
Walk in the promise.
Because with God, the story never ends at the knife.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
